content.value_statement: MCP server projects need consistent patterns for tools, resources, prompts, widgets, authentication, and deployment. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through mcp-use references before implementation.
actual_capabilities: Routes MCP server tasks to focused references for foundations, authentication, server primitives, widgets, and deployment.
Explains when to use tools, resources, prompts, and widgets in mcp-use projects.
Provides setup guidance for new mcp-use servers and existing project changes.
Documents WorkOS, Supabase, and custom OAuth patterns for authenticated MCP servers.
Shows response helper, widget state, interactivity, and UI guidance for production-ready MCP apps.
Includes deployment guidance for Manufact Cloud, self-hosting, Docker, and environment configuration.
limitations: It is a reference skill, not an executable project generator.
It focuses on mcp-use and may not match other MCP frameworks.
Example code still requires review against the target project and dependency versions.
It does not replace security review for production secrets, authentication, or deployment settings.

use_cases.title: Start a new MCP server
use_cases.description: Use the foundation references to scaffold a mcp-use server and choose the first tools, resources, or widgets.

use_cases.title: Add authenticated MCP features
use_cases.description: Follow provider-specific guidance for WorkOS, Supabase, or custom OAuth before adding protected tools.

use_cases.title: Review an MCP app design
use_cases.description: Compare an existing server against mcp-use patterns for responses, widgets, state, and deployment readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a first server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-apps-builder to plan a new mcp-use MCP server for a weather assistant. Read the foundation references first, then list the setup steps and first feature choices.

prompt_templates.title: Add a protected tool
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-apps-builder to add an authenticated tool to an existing mcp-use server. Select the right authentication reference and explain the required environment settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design an interactive widget
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-apps-builder to design an interactive widget for browsing records. Read the widget basics, state, interactivity, and UI guidance before proposing the implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production server
prompt_templates.prompt: Use mcp-apps-builder to review a production mcp-use server for response helpers, authentication, widgets, deployment settings, and common anti-patterns. Return prioritized fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a todo MCP server with a visual list widget.
output: A setup plan for a new mcp-use project.

output_examples.input: Add Supabase authentication to my existing MCP server.
output: Required environment variables and configuration notes.
Implementation steps for protected tool access.
Findings for authentication, errors, widgets, and deployment.
Concrete next steps for production hardening.

best_practices: Read the specific reference file before changing a tool, resource, prompt, widget, or authentication path.
Keep tools focused on one capability and validate all external input with schemas.
Use response helpers, environment variables, and deployment checklists before shipping production servers.
anti_patterns: Do not scaffold inside an unrelated project without confirming the target directory.
Do not hardcode secrets, API keys, provider URLs, or deployment credentials in source files.
Do not build widgets without loading states, theme support, and clear ownership of UI state.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build mcp-use MCP servers with tools, resources, prompts, widgets, authentication, and deployment guidance.

faq.question: Does it generate a complete app automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides the agent to the right references and patterns before implementation.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include authentication guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WorkOS, Supabase, and custom OAuth provider patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with widgets?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes widget basics, state, interactivity, UI guidance, and advanced patterns.

faq.question: Should production code still be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Examples must be checked against project requirements, dependency versions, secrets, and deployment controls.
